{{nihongo|'''Kirishimamine Shrine'''|霧島岑神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto}}<ref name="小林市史3">Kobayashi City History, Vol.3, pp.1095-1097</ref>
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hikohohodemi no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime no Mikoto}}<ref name="小林市史3"/>
* {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|cs|Ugajafukiaezu|es|Ugayafukiaezu|fa|اوگایافوکی‌آئه‌زو|fr|Ugayafukiaezu|id|Ugayafukiaezu|ja|ウガヤフキアエズ|ko|우가야후키아에즈|mni|ꯎꯒꯌꯐꯨꯀꯤꯑꯏꯓꯨ|pl|Ugayafukiaezu|ru|Угаяфукиаэдзу но Микото|simple|Ugayafukiaezu|th|อูงายาฟูกิอาเอซุ|uk|Уґаяфукі-аедзу но мікото|vi|Ugayafukiaezu|zh|鸕鷀草葺不合尊|zh_yue|鸕鶿草葺不合尊|qid=Q1373935|lt=Ugayafukiaezu no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Q3082751|qid=Q3082751|lt=Tamayori-hime no Mikoto}}<ref name="小林市史3"/>
Ninigi, Hikohohodemi, and Ugayafukiaezu are called the {{ill|Three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075|qid=Q56347075}}, ancestors of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|Q909452|qid=Q909452}}, and the other three are their consorts.

=== Origin ===
[[Image:Kirishimamine Jinja Sando.jpg|thumb|270px|Approach]]{{出典の明記| date = 2022年2月| section = 1}}
The founding date is unknown, though tradition places it around the mid-6th century. It is regarded as a shrine deeply connected with the descent of the heavenly grandson ({{ill|Tenson kōrin|Q1084733|qid=Q1084733}}) and the {{ill|Three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075|qid=Q56347075}}{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}.

According to shrine tradition, the "Kirishimamine deity" in the entry for August 1, {{ill|837|Q25093|qid=Q25093}} ({{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|de|Jōwa|es|Jōwa (período Heian)|fa|جووا (دوره هی‌آن)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Heian)|ia|Jowa|id|Jōwa|ja|承和 (日本)|ko|조와 (834년)|ru|Дзёва (Хэйан)|simple|Jōwa (Heian period)|sr|Џова (Хејан период)|tr|Jōwa (Heian)|uk|Дзьова (ненґо)|zh|承和 (日本)|zh_yue|承和|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 4) of the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}'' - where Miyazaki's Tonō, Tsuma, Eda, and Kirishimamine deities were granted status as official shrines - refers to this shrine<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|和書 |title=Miyazaki Prefecture Shrine Records |date=1988-09-30|year=1988|publisher=Miyazaki Prefecture Shrine Office}}</ref>{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}.

In ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'', it is stated that in {{ill|858|Q30371|qid=Q30371}} ({{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 2), it was promoted to Junior Fourth Rank Lower<ref name="小林市史3"/>.

There is also a theory identifying this shrine with "Kirishima Shrine" in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' for Morokata District, Hyuga Province (thus a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=candidate for Engishiki shrine}}){{要出典|date=2022年2月}}.

Originally it was enshrined at "Setao" (Semonto Hill / Setoo), between {{ill|Mount Takachiho|Q3514128|qid=Q3514128}} and {{ill|Ohachi|Q11489346|qid=Q11489346|lt=Hiwa-ga-mine (Miike)}}, in present-day {{ill|Takaharu, Miyazaki|Q1206617|qid=Q1206617}}, Nishimorokata District, Miyazaki. It was therefore also called '''Setao Gongen''', and its betto temple was said to be Setao-ji<ref name="小林市史3"/>.

Around the Tenkei and Tenryaku eras, priest {{ill|Shōkū|Q11491623|qid=Q11491623}} is said to have founded four other shrines including Himamori Shrine around the mountain foothills, and together with Kirishimamine Shrine (also called the Central Gongen Shrine of Mt. Kirishima) they were called the {{ill|Kirishima Rokusha Gongen|Q11660872|qid=Q11660872}}. During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|de|Shinbutsu-Shūgō|es|Shinbutsu shūgō|eu|Shinbutsu-shūgō|fa|شینبوتسو-شوگو|fi|Shinbutsu shūgō|fr|Shinbutsu shūgō|id|Shinbutsu-shūgō|it|Shinbutsu shūgō|ja|神仏習合|ko|신불습합|pl|Synkretyzm shintō-buddyjski|ru|Синто-буддийский синкретизм|th|ชิมบุตสึชูโง|tr|Şinbutsu-şuugō|uk|Синто-буддистський синкретизм|ur|شنتو اور بدھ مت کا امتزاج ضدین|zh|神佛習合|qid=Q2279088}}, {{ill|Vairocana|Q239847|qid=Q239847}} was enshrined at Setao-ji on the approach, and the shrine came to be called '''Kirishima-san Chuo Rokusho (Rokusha) Gongen''' ('''Kirishimamine Shrine''')<ref name="小林市史3"/>. As the name suggests, it became the center of the {{ill|Kirishima Rokusha Gongen|Q11660872|qid=Q11660872}}, and Kirishima worship flourished.

In {{ill|1112|Q19525|qid=Q19525}} ({{ill|Ten'ei|Q1193915|qid=Q1193915}} 3), eruption of {{ill|Mount Karakuni|Q3321904|qid=Q3321904}}, and in {{ill|1167|Q19678|qid=Q19678}} ({{ill|Nin'an|Q3577285|qid=Q3577285|lt=Nin'an}} 2), eruption of Ōhata-yama burned shrine buildings, but each time they were rebuilt on the original site. In {{ill|1234|ab|1234|abstract|Q5424|af|1234|als|1234|am|1234 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1234|ar|1234|ary|1234|arz|1234|ast|1234|avk|1234|az|1234|azb|۱۲۳۴ (میلادی)|be|1234|be_x_old|1234|bg|1234|bn|১২৩৪|bpy|মারি ১২৩৪|br|1234|bs|1234.|ca|1234|cdo|1234 nièng|ceb|1234|ckb|١٢٣٤|crh|1234|cs|1234|cv|1234|cy|1234|da|1234|de|1234|diq|1234|el|1234|eml|1234|eo|1234|es|1234|et|1234|eu|1234|fa|۱۲۳۴ (میلادی)|fi|1234|fo|1234|fr|1234|frr|1234|fy|1234|ga|1234|gan|1234年|gcr|1234|gd|1234|gl|1234|he|1234|hi|१२३४|hr|1234.|ht|1234 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1234|hy|1234|id|1234|ilo|1234|io|1234|is|1234|it|1234|ja|1234年|jv|1234|ka|1234|kaa|1234|kk|1234 жыл|ko|1234년|la|1234|lb|1234|lij|1234|lmo|1234|lt|1234 m.|lv|1234. gads|map_bms|1234|mdf|1234|mg|1234|mhr|1234|mi|1234|min|1234|mk|1234|mr|इ.स. १२३४|mrj|1234 и|ms|1234|my|၁၂၃၄|mzn|۱۲۳۴|nah|1234|nap|1234|nds|1234|new|सन् १२३४|nl|1234|nn|1234|no|1234|nrm|1234|nso|1234|oc|1234|or|୧୨୩୪|os|1234-æм аз|pa|੧੨੩੪|pl|1234|pnb|1234|pt|1234|qu|1234|ro|1234|ru|1234 год|rue|1234|sa|१२३४|sah|1234|scn|1234|sd|1234ع|se|1234|sh|1234.|shn|1234|simple|1234|sk|1234|sl|1234|smn|1234|sq|1234|sr|1234|su|1234|sv|1234|sw|1234|tg|Соли 1234|th|พ.ศ. 1777|tk|1234|tl|1234|tly|1234|tr|1234|tt|1234 ел|uk|1234|ur|1234ء|uz|1234|vec|1234|vi|1234|war|1234|wuu|1234年|xmf|1234|zea|1234|zh|1234年|zh_min_nan|1234 nî|zh_yue|1234年|qid=Q5424}} ({{ill|Bunryaku|Q1194125|qid=Q1194125}} 1), a nearby eruption of {{ill|Ohachi|Q11489346|qid=Q11489346|lt=Hiwa-ga-mine (Miike)}} again burned the shrine, and because a spring called Ama-no-I from this highland site dried up, it was moved near the branch shrine Kiribe Ōji Shrine, and that place was called "Shin-Setao"<ref name="小林市史3"/>.

However, in {{ill|1716|Q6892|qid=Q6892}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} 1), eruption of {{ill|Shinmoedake|Q514392|qid=Q514392}} burned it again. The sacred body was first moved to Imabo Gongen and then to Okahara in Hosono village, but as the "Shin-Setao" site became completely deserted, in {{ill|1729|Q6952|qid=Q6952}} (Kyoho 14) shrine buildings were rebuilt on the mid-slope of {{ill|Hinamori Dake|Q10942052|qid=Q10942052}} and remained there until early Meiji. That location is still called Tsukiji<ref name=":0" />{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}.

It was ranked as {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}} in {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), and after combining {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hinamori Shrine}} (also counted among {{ill|Kirishima Rokusha Gongen|Q11660872|qid=Q11660872}}) in {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), it was moved to the former site of Hinamori Shrine (present location), where it remains today<ref name="小林市史3"/>.

In ''{{ill|Sangoku meisho zue|Q11354726|qid=Q11354726}}'', a record of famous places in {{ill|Satsuma Domain|Q676187|qid=Q676187}}, it is written as "'''Kirishima Dai-gongen-gu'''".

Since ancient times it flourished as a noted shrine worshipped by the clans that ruled this area, including the {{ill|Shimazu clan|Q1061406|qid=Q1061406}}, {{ill|Itō clan|Q2975280|qid=Q2975280}}, and {{ill|Kitahara clan|ja|北原氏|qid=Q11401254}}. {{ill|Shimazu Yoshihiro|ban|Shimazu Yoshihiro|ca|Shimazu Yoshihiro|de|Shimazu Yoshihiro|es|Shimazu Yoshihiro|fa|شیمازو یوشی‌هیرو|fi|Shimazu Yoshihiro|fr|Shimazu Yoshihiro|id|Shimazu Yoshihiro|it|Shimazu Yoshihiro|ja|島津義弘|ko|시마즈 요시히로|mr|योशिहिरो शिमाझु|nl|Shimazu Yoshihiro|pt|Shimazu Yoshihiro|ru|Симадзу Ёсихиро|th|ชิมาซุ โยชิฮิโระ|tr|Shimazu Yoshihiro|uk|Сімадзу Йосіхіро|vi|Shimazu Yoshihiro|zh|島津義弘|zh_min_nan|Simazu Yosihiro|qid=Q1156288}} is also said to have worshipped here while based at {{ill|Iino Castle|ja|飯野城|qid=Q11666711}}, and to have donated 100 hyo of rice each year as shrine lands<ref name="小林市史3"/>.
